name: Saint Martin's Island
tagline: The only coral island of Bangladesh — turquoise water & coconut palms.

cover.alt: Wooden fishing boats on turquoise water off the palm-lined shore of Saint Martin's Island
cover.caption: Fishing boats off the island

overview.intro: Saint Martin's Island is a small island of about 8 km² in the Bay of Bengal, around 9 km south of the mainland tip at Teknaf. Locals also call it Narikel Jinjira, 'Coconut Island'. It is the only coral island in Bangladesh, with clear blue-green water, rocky coral shores and rows of coconut palms. There are no cars — you walk, cycle or ride a battery van. Because the coral and sea-turtle habitat are fragile, the government now strictly limits tourism: the island is open only for a few months a year, daily visitor numbers are capped, and you need an online travel pass. These rules change every season, so always check the latest government notice before you book anything.
highlights: Turquoise water and coral-stone beaches on the west side of the island
Chhera Dwip — the tiny southern tip, cut off at high tide, the southernmost land of Bangladesh
Sunset over the sea from the West Beach
Cycling or walking the full ring of the island (about 3–4 hrs)
Fresh fish BBQ and green coconuts (daab) straight from the trees
Starry, quiet nights with no city lights (when overnight stays are allowed)
overview.bestTimeSummary: December – January (when tourist access is open; rules change every season)

seasons.name: Early Season
seasons.weather: Dry and sunny, sea calming down after the monsoon. In recent seasons November was open for day trips only (no overnight stays). Check the current notice.

seasons.name: Peak (Open Season)
seasons.weather: Cool, dry and calm — the best sea conditions. In recent seasons overnight stays were allowed in these months, with a daily visitor cap (around 2,000 people).

seasons.name: Closed to Tourists
seasons.weather: Pleasant to hot, but in recent seasons tourist ships stopped from February to protect the island's ecosystem and turtle nesting.

seasons.name: Monsoon & Cyclone Season
seasons.weather: Rough sea, heavy rain and cyclone risk. Tourist ships do not run.

howToReach.summary: It is a two-part trip. First get from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar by train, bus or flight. Then take a licensed tourist ship to the island. In recent seasons ships left from the BIWTA jetty at Nuniachhara in Cox's Bazar (about 6–7 hrs each way), because the shorter Teknaf route was closed for security reasons. Ships leave early in the morning, so plan to spend the night before in Cox's Bazar. Ship tickets, the travel pass and departure points change every season — check the latest notice first.
howToReach.distanceFromDhaka: ~400 km to Cox's Bazar, then ~120 km by sea (≈9 km from Teknaf)

routes.label: Train to Cox's Bazar + Ship (Recommended)
routes.totalTime: ~1.5 days (incl. one night in Cox's Bazar)

steps.title: Register online and get your travel pass
steps.description: In recent seasons every visitor needed an online registration / travel pass (with a QR code) linked to a ship ticket. Buy ship tickets only through the official portal or the ship company — numbers are capped each day.
steps.tip: Do this BEFORE you book your train. If you cannot get a ship date, the rest of the plan falls apart.

steps.title: Train from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar
steps.description: The Cox's Bazar Express (overnight) or Parjatak Express (daytime) leaves Kamalapur Railway Station and also stops at Biman Bandar (Airport) station.
steps.tip: Book on eticket.railway.gov.bd exactly when sales open, 10 days before travel.

steps.title: Night in Cox's Bazar
steps.description: Ships leave around 7 AM, so stay the night in Kolatoli or near the Nuniachhara jetty. See our Cox's Bazar guide for hotels.

steps.title: CNG to the BIWTA jetty, Nuniachhara
steps.description: The jetty is at the north end of Cox's Bazar town. Arrive at least 45 minutes early for ticket and travel-pass checks.

steps.title: Ship to Saint Martin's Island
steps.description: Large tourist ships (sea-going vessels with seats, open decks and some cabins) sail down the coast to the island jetty. Ships usually arrive in the early afternoon.
steps.tip: Take seasickness tablets 30 minutes before boarding if you are prone to it. Sit near the middle of the ship.

routes.label: Overnight Bus to Cox's Bazar + Ship (Cheapest)
routes.totalTime: ~1.5 days (incl. one night in Cox's Bazar)

steps.title: Overnight coach to Cox's Bazar
steps.description: AC buses (Green Line, Shyamoli NR, Hanif, Saint Martin Hyundai) leave Dhaka counters at Arambagh, Fakirapool, Sayedabad and Kalabagan between 9 and 11 PM.

steps.title: Day and night in Cox's Bazar
steps.description: You arrive in the morning, too late for that day's ship. Enjoy the beach and sleep in Cox's Bazar.

steps.title: CNG to the BIWTA jetty, Nuniachhara
steps.description: Leave your hotel by about 6 AM. Carry your passport/NID and printed or phone copy of the travel pass.

steps.title: Ship to Saint Martin's Island
steps.description: About 6–7 hrs along the coast. Food and tea are sold on board, but bring water and snacks.

steps.title: Flight DAC → CXB
steps.description: Biman Bangladesh, US-Bangla, Novoair and Air Astra fly several times a day from the domestic terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
steps.tip: Take an afternoon or evening flight the day before your ship. Morning flights land too late for the 7 AM departure.

steps.title: CNG to your Cox's Bazar hotel
steps.description: The airport is in town. Choose a hotel near Kolatoli or the north end of town for an easy early start.

steps.title: CNG to the BIWTA jetty, Nuniachhara
steps.description: Arrive at least 45 minutes before departure for checks.

steps.title: Ship to Saint Martin's Island
steps.description: Pick a cabin or business-class seat if you want more comfort on the long ride.

transportOptions.name: Tourist ships from Cox's Bazar (e.g. Karnafuly Express, Bay One and others)
transportOptions.bookingTip: Buy only via the official travel-pass portal or the ship company. Ships and fares change each season; avoid touts selling 'guaranteed' tickets.

transportOptions.name: Ships from Teknaf (when the route is open)

classes.name: Seat (return)
classes.note: Approx. This route was closed in recent seasons for security reasons on the Naf River.

transportOptions.bookingTip: Shorter and cheaper, but only use it if the season's notice says Teknaf departures are allowed.

transportOptions.name: Cox's Bazar Express / Parjatak Express (Dhaka → Cox's Bazar)
transportOptions.departFrom: Kamalapur Railway Station (also Biman Bandar / Airport station)
transportOptions.bookingTip: Book at eticket.railway.gov.bd (foreigners can register with a passport). Sales open 10 days ahead.

transportOptions.name: Green Line / Shyamoli NR / Hanif / Saint Martin Hyundai
transportOptions.departFrom: Arambagh, Fakirapool, Sayedabad or Kalabagan counters
transportOptions.bookingTip: Book online at shohoz.com or bdtickets.com. Some companies sell bus + ship combo tickets in season — check they include a valid travel pass.

transportOptions.name: Biman / US-Bangla / Novoair / Air Astra to Cox's Bazar
transportOptions.departFrom: Hazrat Shahjalal Int'l Airport — Domestic Terminal

classes.name: Economy
classes.note: Prices rise sharply in December holidays.

transportOptions.bookingTip: Book 2+ weeks ahead on the airline's website or GoZayaan / ShareTrip.

lastMile.note: Price per vehicle. Book the CNG the night before for a 6 AM pickup.
Battery vans and rickshaw-vans wait at the jetty. Many places are walkable — ask your hotel for directions.
Walk or cycle along the beach at low tide only. Easy-bikes go part of the way (about BDT 300–600 per vehicle, approx.). Local boats also run (approx. BDT 200–300 per person).
Bicycles can be rented (approx. BDT 100–150 per hour) — the best way to explore.

budget.disclaimer: Prices were checked for the 2025–26 season and are approximate. Ship fares, the travel pass and whether overnight stays are allowed change every season. Late December is the most expensive time.

tiers.label: Budget Backpacker
tiers.roundTripMode: Shovan Chair train or non-AC bus + open-deck ship
tiers.notes: Simple cottage with fan, local rice-and-fish meals, walking and cycling.

tiers.label: Mid-Range Comfort
tiers.roundTripMode: Snigdha (AC) train or AC bus + business-class ship seat
tiers.notes: Resort room with attached bathroom and generator/solar power, fish BBQ dinners, easy-bike to Chhera Dwip.

tiers.label: Best Available
tiers.roundTripMode: Return flight to Cox's Bazar + ship cabin
tiers.notes: The island has no true 5-star hotels. This means the best sea-view resort, a private cabin on the ship and good seafood meals.

entryFees.note: No separate entry fee in recent seasons, but the online travel pass is mandatory. Any fee is usually included in the ship ticket — check.
Free, day visits only. Protected area — no overnight stays.
Any terminal charge is usually included in the ship ticket (approx.).

stay.name: Local family cottages
stay.why: Simple rooms run by island families. Cheap and walkable to the bazar and North Beach.
stay.bookingTip: Power is from solar or a generator and may only run in the evening. Ask before booking.

stay.name: Eco-cottages on the West Beach
stay.why: Bamboo-and-thatch cottages under coconut palms, steps from the best sunset spot.

stay.name: Blue Marine Resort
stay.why: One of the island's larger, more established resorts, with a restaurant and attached bathrooms.

stay.name: Samudra Bilas
stay.why: The seaside house built by the famous writer Humayun Ahmed, now rented out as guest rooms. Quiet, with direct beach views.
stay.bookingTip: Very popular — book as soon as you have your ship date.

stay.name: Prasad Paradise Resort
stay.why: One of the most comfortable resorts on the island, with sea-view rooms and an on-site restaurant. Not 5-star, but the best available.

stay.name: Sayeman Beach Resort (before/after the ship)
stay.why: If overnight stays on the island are not allowed, base yourself here and do a day trip. Sea-view infinity pool and easy access to the jetty.

dishes.name: Fresh Fish BBQ
dishes.description: Pick a fish (rupchanda, surma, red snapper) at an evening stall in the bazar and it is grilled with spices. Prices are by size or weight.

dishes.name: Lobster & Crab
dishes.description: Cooked masala-style or grilled. Prices are by weight, so ask first.

dishes.name: Green Coconut
dishes.description: The island is covered in coconut palms. Cold daab water is the best drink in the heat — and safe, because it is opened in front of you.

dishes.name: Rupchanda Fry with Rice & Bhorta
dishes.description: Silver pomfret fried with turmeric and chilli, served with rice, dal and mashed vegetable bhorta. A simple, filling lunch.

dishes.name: Shutki (Dried Fish)
dishes.description: Fish dried on racks along the shore. Try it as a spicy bhuna, or buy a packet to take home.

spots.name: Main bazar restaurants
spots.knownFor: Rice, fish curry, dal and bhorta thali

spots.name: Evening BBQ stalls
spots.knownFor: Pick-your-own fish, crab and lobster grilled to order

spots.name: Resort restaurants (Blue Marine, Prasad Paradise)
spots.knownFor: Cleaner kitchens, set menus and seafood

safetyTips: Drink only sealed bottled water. Island tap and well water is not safe for visitors.
Agree on the price per kg and the cooking charge BEFORE the fish goes on the grill.
Eat seafood that is cooked through, and freshly grilled rather than reheated.
Bring some snacks and ORS ('Orsaline'). Choice and supplies on the island are limited.

items: Rules change every season. Always check the latest government (Ministry of Environment / BIWTA / Cox's Bazar district) notice before booking.
In recent seasons: open only about November to January, a cap of around 2,000 visitors a day, an online travel pass with QR code required, and in some months day trips only (no overnight stays).
Carry your passport (foreigners) or NID (locals). Your ID is checked against the travel pass at the jetty.
Never try to reach the island on fishing trawlers or speedboats. It is illegal for tourists and dangerous on the open sea.
No single-use plastic. Bring a refillable bottle and take your rubbish back to the mainland.
Do not touch, break or collect coral, shells, starfish or rocks. Fines apply.
No loud music, bonfires, barbecues or bright lights on the beach at night — sea turtles come ashore to nest.
Chhera Dwip is a protected area: no camping, no overnight stays, and no motorised vehicles on the beach.
Coral rocks are sharp. Wear sandals or water shoes in the water and on the rocky shores.
Check tide times before walking to Chhera Dwip. The rising tide cuts it off from the main island.
Swim only in calm, sandy spots, never alone and never after dark. There are no lifeguards.
Ships are cancelled when cyclone or storm signals are raised. Keep a spare day in your plan.
The Myanmar border is close. Do not go near the Naf River border area or follow anyone offering 'border tours'.
The island is a conservative fishing community. Most locals swim fully clothed.
Women: a T-shirt and shorts or leggings over swimwear attracts the least attention.
Ask before photographing people, especially women and children.
Mobile data (Grameenphone, Robi) works on most of the island but can be slow.
Electricity is mostly solar or generator power, often only at certain hours. Bring a power bank.
Do not rely on ATMs or cards on the island. Bring enough cash from Cox's Bazar.

itinerary.title: Ship from Cox's Bazar & West Beach Sunset

activities.activity: CNG from your Cox's Bazar hotel to the BIWTA jetty at Nuniachhara. Show your travel pass and board the ship.
activities.tip: Bring water, snacks, sunscreen and seasickness tablets for the 6–7 hr ride.

activities.activity: Arrive at the island jetty. Easy-bike or walk to your cottage, then a late seafood lunch at the bazar.
Walk to the West Beach for sunset over the open sea.
activities.tip: Turn off torches near the waterline after dark to protect nesting turtles.

activities.activity: Fish BBQ dinner and a quiet look at the stars.

itinerary.overnight: Saint Martin's Island cottage (if overnight stays are allowed)

activities.activity: Walk or cycle south along the beach to Chhera Dwip at low tide. Rock pools, coral stones and the southern tip of Bangladesh.
activities.tip: Check the tide table with your hotel the night before. Start back before the tide turns.

activities.activity: Back for lunch and rest in the shade — the midday sun is very strong.
Rent a bicycle and ride round the rest of the island: Golachipa, the coconut groves and the North Beach.
Green coconut at sunset and an early night.

itinerary.title: Morning Swim & Ship Back

activities.activity: Swim or snorkel-look in a calm sandy spot near the West or North Beach. Buy shutki or coconut snacks as gifts.
Board the return ship at the island jetty (check the exact time on your ticket).
Arrive in Cox's Bazar around 9–10 PM. Stay overnight or take a night bus back to Dhaka.
activities.tip: If overnight stays on the island are not allowed this season, do Day 1 and Day 3 as a single day trip and stay in Cox's Bazar.

itinerary.overnight: Cox's Bazar hotel / night bus to Dhaka
